# MM-P2-L2-RR03-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Scope
- Purpose: Provide standardized instructions for inspection, verification, and application of torque to structural and rotating machine fasteners on the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03). This procedure focuses on fasteners that affect safety, rigging, alignment, and load transfer on the mill, including roll housings, radial arms, gearbox housings, and guard and access panels.
- Applicability: Maintenance and reliability technicians, mill electricians, and the shift lead responsible for startup clearance prior to production. Use in conjunction with referenced system and safety procedures listed in Related documents.

Background and rationale
- Fastener integrity is critical for dimensional stability, operator safety, and preventing unplanned downtime. Loss of preload or improper torque can permit fretting, fatigue cracking, and component movement that propagates into the ring forming process. Inspection combined with controlled re-torquing restores clamp load and documents machine condition.
- The mill processes rings up to the maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 1525 mm. Components and fastener choices are sized and selected to support these workpiece dimensions; maintain fastener integrity accordingly.
- Lubrication of bearing and gearbox interfaces is governed by the plant lubrication schedule. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is CFW-LUB-101. Use only the specified lubricant in gearbox and bearing fill operations; record part numbers used in maintenance records.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench suitable for industrial fasteners and traceable to calibration records.
- Torque multipliers and reaction bars for inaccessible or high-preload bolting locations.
- Dial or digital tension indicator for verification where specified by OEM or critical joints.
- Clean lint-free rags, solvent approved by plant material safety, and anti-seize compound specified by OEM or plant lubrication policy.
- Fastener identification tags and durable marker for marking inspected and torqued hardware.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for concealed head and thread inspection.
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P2-L2-01 and plant safety policies.

Procedure
- Pre-inspection actions:
  - Obtain machine isolation following lockout-tagout procedures referenced in SOP-P2-L2-01. Confirm power and stored energy isolation before any work near rotating parts.
  - Review last maintenance history and fastener records. Consult SB-1049 for any safety bulletins affecting fastener assemblies or threadlocker usage on this equipment.
  - Verify tool calibration status and ensure torque wrench calibration traceability is available for attachment to the work order.

- Visual inspection:
  - Inspect each accessible fastener for thread exposure, head condition, corrosion, and evidence of movement such as paint witness marks that do not align. Use mirror or borescope for concealed heads.
  - Inspect mating surfaces for signs of bearing movement, fretting, or contact wear that could indicate preload loss.
  - For flange interfaces and guard mounts, verify gasket or spacer condition; replace if deformation or extrusion is present.

- Marking and documentation:
  - Mark each fastener head with a durable tag or marker to indicate inspection status and technician initials. Record fastener location, head type, and any observed anomalies on the maintenance record.
  - Note lubricant part number used on records when lubrication tasks are performed: CFW-LUB-101.

- Torque verification and application:
  - Where joint design and access allow, verify preload using calibrated tools. If preload verification indicates acceptable clamp load, note result on record and proceed to next fastener.
  - When re-torquing is required due to evidence of preload loss or per engineering direction, apply torque using calibrated equipment. Use reaction bars and multipliers to prevent tool drift and ensure safe application.
  - For critical rotating joints and structural connections, follow OEM recommendations for sequence and method of achieving final clamp load. If OEM guidance is not available, use progressive and symmetrical tightening to re-establish even joint compression.
  - After torque application, mark heads or tags to indicate final torque verification and sign the record.

- Special cases and safety considerations:
  - For studs welded into housings or pressed-in anchor studs, do not apply external torque that could induce shear; consult engineering and SB-1049 before any corrective action.
  - If a fastener shows thread damage, head rounding, or evidence of fatigue, remove and replace the fastener. Record replacement and reason on the maintenance log. Use OEM-specified replacement parts, and confirm compatibility with structural loads.
  - For joints with specified lubricant or thread treatment, apply thread compound per product data and SOP-P2-L2-05 before installation.

Acceptance criteria
- Fasteners inspected and documented as compliant have:
  - No visible thread damage or head deformation.
  - Witness marks or stamp indicators showing no relative movement after torque confirmation.
  - Maintenance record entries with location, technician initials, method used for verification, and lubricant part number when applicable: CFW-LUB-101.
- Fasteners requiring replacement or further engineering review are those with damaged threads, signs of fatigue cracking, or weld damage at stud bases; these items must be tagged out and escalated to maintenance engineering and recorded.
- All re-torqued joints shall show evidence of verification on the maintenance record and be signed by the performing technician and the shift lead prior to machine release for production.

Records to keep
- Complete maintenance record for the inspection event, including fastener locations, inspection findings, torque verification method, and signatures. Attach torque tool calibration certificate for traceability.
- Parts used record showing replacement fastener part numbers, and lubricant usage recorded with exact part number: CFW-LUB-101.
- Any deviation reports and engineering dispositions referencing SB-1049 where safety bulletins or deviations were applied.

Related documents
- SB-1049
- SOP-P2-L2-01
- SOP-P2-L2-05

Notes
- Follow site-specific safety and PPE requirements. Do not operate machine until sign-off is obtained on the maintenance record.
